summary: Compare tentative distances with settled shortest distances while stepping edge relaxations.
objective: Make a weighted directed graph with editable nonnegative costs and let me inspect each Dijkstra relaxation and priority-queue change.

entities.name: Weighted digraph
entities.guidance: Use labeled node pedestals and directional edge arrows; costs are text badges rather than geometric lengths.

entities.name: Relaxation comparator
entities.guidance: For the active edge u->v display dist[u]+w(u,v) beside current dist[v], including infinity as a symbolic value.

entities.name: Priority queue and tree
entities.guidance: List tentative keys in priority order and highlight the evolving predecessor tree separately from scanned edges.

state_contract.model: Finite directed graph, finite weights >=0, source distance zero and others infinity. Extract minimum unsettled tentative distance; relax outgoing edges and update predecessors on strict improvement.
state_contract.authority: The graph model and priority-queue algorithm own all distances and settled flags. A deterministic tie policy makes replay reproducible.
actions: Set source and nonnegative edge weights before execution.
Select a destination and reconstruct its current or final path.

invariants: Settled distances do not subsequently improve under the stated assumptions.
Successful relaxation strictly lowers the tentative distance and updates its predecessor consistently.
Unreachable nodes keep infinity; stale queue entries are ignored if a duplicate-entry heap implementation is used.
motion_guidance: Animate key movement after an actual decrease; never move a token to suggest an improvement that did not occur.
Show tentative paths as provisional until the destination is settled.
known_limits: Negative edge weights are rejected; use an appropriate different algorithm for that case.
Zero-weight edges are allowed, but equal-distance tie choices can produce different valid trees.
Curated recipe only; no runtime scene or rendered behavior has been verified for this record.

claims.statement: Dijkstra algorithm solves the single-source shortest-path problem for edge-weighted directed graphs with nonnegative weights.
claims.scope: The nonnegative-weight precondition is essential to the settling rule.

object_craft.structure: Use labeled node pedestals and directional edge arrows; costs are text badges rather than geometric lengths.
object_craft.material: Neutral graph geometry with strong edge direction and readable cost labels; distinct outlines separate tentative from settled state.
